read.passage: Last month, students at a school in Dammam had a class debate. The question was: 'Should students be allowed to use phones at break time?' Fahad was convinced that phones are useful. He said, 'In my opinion, we can use them to call our parents or check our homework.' His classmate Nawaf didn't agree. 'I see your point,' he said, 'but if everyone looks at a phone, nobody will play or talk.' In the end, the teacher gave some advice: 'If I were you, I'd keep phones in your bags at break and use them only after school.' Most students said that the idea made sense, so the class came to an agreement.

qs.q: Why does Fahad think phones are useful?
options: Students can call their parents or check homework.
qs.cando: Can understand articles and reports about school and everyday life.

read2.passage: Should Schools Start Later? Many teenagers find it hard to get up early, and scientists say there is a reason. During the teenage years, the body clock changes, so teenagers often feel sleepy later at night. If school starts at seven, many students arrive tired. Some schools in other countries have tried starting an hour later. Teachers there say students are more awake and get better marks. However, not everyone agrees. Some parents say a later start would make it difficult for them to drive their children to school before work. In my opinion, schools should try it for one term and then ask students and parents what they think.
